evidence.summary: [agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/api/Users -> 401. Unauthenticated GET /api/Users returns 401, but the same request as ordinary customer athz1 (user id 25) returns HTTP 200 with the full Users table (~10.7KB) including other users' ids, emails, roles (admin/deluxe/accounting) and deluxeTokens. Authentication is required but authorization is not scoped — a customer can read the admin-only user collection (broken function-level authorization).

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/api/Users as test account athz1 -> 200. Unauthenticated GET /api/Users returns 401, but the same request as ordinary customer athz1 (user id 25) returns HTTP 200 with the full Users table (~10.7KB) including other users' ids, emails, roles (admin/deluxe/accounting) and deluxeTokens. Authentication is required but authorization is not scoped — a customer can read the admin-only user collection (broken function-level authorization). [36 values redacted: email address]

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/api/Users/1 as test account athz1 -> 200. As customer athz1 (id 25), GET /api/Users/1 returned HTTP 200 with admin id 1's record, and GET /api/Users/26 returned the record of the other test account athz2 (id 26). The per-id user endpoint applies no ownership check, letting any customer read arbitrary users' records (IDOR/BOLA). [1 value redacted: email address]

As customer athz1 (id 25), GET /api/Users/1 returned HTTP 200 with admin id 1's record, and GET /api/Users/26 returned the record of the other test account athz2 (id 26). The per-id user endpoint applies no ownership check, letting any customer read arbitrary users' records (IDOR/BOLA). [1 value redacted: email address]

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/rest/user/authentication-details as test account athz1 -> 200. As customer athz1, GET /rest/user/authentication-details returned HTTP 200 (~13.7KB) enumerating every user's id, email, password hash and totpSecret rather than only the caller's — authorization not scoped to caller. By contrast GET /rest/order-history/orders (admin-only) returned 403 "Malicious activity detected", showing that endpoint does enforce role. [36 values redacted: email address]

By contrast GET /rest/order-history/orders (admin-only) returned 403 "Malicious activity detected", showing that endpoint does enforce role.

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/rest/basket/1 as test account athz1 -> 200. As customer athz1 (user id 25), GET /rest/basket/1 returned HTTP 200 with basket id 1 belonging to UserId 1 (admin); as athz2 (user id 26), GET /rest/basket/2 returned basket id 2 belonging to UserId 2. Neither account owns the basket it retrieved, confirming /rest/basket/:id has no ownership check (IDOR on shopping baskets).

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/rest/basket/2 as test account athz2 -> 200. As customer athz1 (user id 25), GET /rest/basket/1 returned HTTP 200 with basket id 1 belonging to UserId 1 (admin); as athz2 (user id 26), GET /rest/basket/2 returned basket id 2 belonging to UserId 2. Neither account owns the basket it retrieved, confirming /rest/basket/:id has no ownership check (IDOR on shopping baskets).

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/ftp/package.json.bak -> 403. GET /ftp/package.json.bak returns 403 "Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!" (with a verbose fileServer.js stack trace), but GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md (URL-encoded null byte) returns HTTP 200, Content-Type application/octet-stream, 4263 bytes — the full backup file including the jsonwebtoken dependency value. The poison null byte truncates the served path past the extension allowlist, allowing retrieval of non-.md/.pdf files.

The poison null byte truncates the served path past the extension allowlist, allowing retrieval of non-.md/.pdf files. [2 values redacted: jsonwebtoken, email address]

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/ftp/..%2fpackage.json -> 403. GET /ftp/..%2fpackage.json returned 403 Forbidden (serve-index blocks the ../ traversal), but GET /ftp/coupons_2013.md.bak%2500.md returned HTTP 200 with the encoded coupons backup (131 bytes), confirming the null-byte extension-allowlist bypass works across multiple restricted /ftp files while plain directory traversal is rejected.

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/rest/basket/2 as test account athz1 -> 200. As customer athz1, GET /rest/basket/2 returned HTTP 200 with basket id 2 (UserId 2), a second foreign basket — confirming athz1 can enumerate and read multiple other users' baskets, not just one.

[agent] POST http://juice.lab.test/api/Users -> 201. Sent once by the gateway after a lab write rule approved it: lab write rule #9 (made by the operator token) approved it on 2026-10-16 20:41 UTC, not a person reading this request; separation of duties not met: the rule's maker also started the run (write 54, request SHA-256 d89de7310d4e). Agent's reason: Test privilege escalation via mass assignment: unauthenticated registration honoring a client-supplied role=admin. Uses a freshly generated account, not a seeded one.. [2 values redacted: email address, password]

Agent's reason: Test vertical privilege escalation via mass assignment: whether customer athz1 can PATCH its own user record (id 25) to role=admin. Operates only on the test account's own record..

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/api/Users?sort=-id&limit=3 as test account athz1 -> 200. Privilege escalation via mass assignment: unauthenticated POST /api/Users with {"role":"admin"} returned 201 and created user id 39 with role "admin" and profileImage defaultAdmin.png (verified in the sort=-id listing x18, createdAt 2026-10-16T20:41:17 matching the request). By contrast, attempting vertical escalation of an existing account via PATCH /api/Users/25 {"role":"admin"} as athz1 returned HTTP 500 and GET /api/Users/25 shows role still "customer" — that update vector is blocked, but registration role injection succeeds. [37 values redacted: email address]

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/api/BasketItems/1 as test account athz1 -> 200. As customer athz1, GET /api/BasketItems/1 returned HTTP 200 with basket item id 1 belonging to BasketId 1 (admin's basket) — IDOR on basket items. By contrast GET /api/Addresss/1 and GET /api/Cards/1 both returned 400 "Malicious activity detected", showing those per-id endpoints do enforce an ownership/anti-IDOR check while BasketItems does not.
